claim: Ribosome biogenesis is a vital and highly energy-consuming cellular function occurring primarily in the nucleolus.
source: Ribosome biogenesis is a vital and highly energy-consuming cellular function occurring primarily in the nucleolus.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the nucleolus and ribosome biogenesis.

claim: Cancer cells have an elevated demand for ribosomes to sustain continuous proliferation.
source: Cancer cells have an elevated demand for ribosomes to sustain continuous proliferation.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about cancer cell metabolism.

claim: A novel parameter termed 'nucleolar normality score' was developed that measures the ratio of the fibrillar center and granular component proteins in the nucleolus and nucleoplasm.
source: For a readout, a novel parameter termed 'nucleolar normality score' was developed that measures the ratio of the fibrillar center and granular component proteins in the nucleolus and nucleoplasm.
evidence: The manuscript describes the development and methodology of this novel parameter.

claim: Multiple classes of drugs were found to induce nucleolar stress, including DNA intercalators, inhibitors of mTOR/PI3K, heat shock proteins, proteasome, and cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs).
source: Multiple classes of drugs were found to induce nucleolar stress, including DNA intercalators, inhibitors of mTOR/PI3K, heat shock proteins, proteasome, and cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the screening study presented in the manuscript.

claim: Each class of drugs induced morphologically and molecularly distinct states of nucleolar stress accompanied by changes in nucleolar biophysical properties.
source: Each class of drugs induced morphologically and molecularly distinct states of nucleolar stress accompanied by changes in nucleolar biophysical properties.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the characterization studies in the manuscript.

claim: Multiple CDK substrates were identified in the nucleolus, including RNA Pol I–recruiting protein Treacle, which was phosphorylated by CDK9 in vitro.
source: Multiple CDK substrates were identified in the nucleolus, including RNA Pol I– recruiting protein Treacle, which was phosphorylated by CDK9 in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by phosphoproteomics data and in vitro kinase assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: The results revealed a concerted regulation of RNA Pol I and Pol II by transcriptional CDKs.
source: These results revealed a concerted regulation of RNA Pol I and Pol II by transcriptional CDKs.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental findings regarding CDK9 activity.

claim: Rapidly proliferating cancer cells have ribosome biogenesis shifted into overdrive, which may be one of their primary metabolic alterations.
source: Rapidly proliferating cancer cells have ribosome biogenesis shifted into overdrive, which may be one of their primary metabolic alterations (Drygin et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The nucleolus is a membrane-less organelle that assembles around ribosomal RNA genes (rDNA).
source: The nucleolus is a membrane-less organelle that assembles around ribosomal RNA genes (rDNA).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about nucleolar structure.

claim: rRNA genes in eukaryotic cells are present in hundreds of tandemly arranged repetitive copies that are transcribed by RNA polymerase I (Pol I).
source: rRNA genes in eukaryotic cells are present in hundreds of tandemly arranged repetitive copies that are transcribed by RNA polymerase I (Pol I) (reviewed in Potapova and Gerton, 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Nucleolar anatomy in animal cells is comprised of three distinct compartments: the fibrillar center (FC), the dense fibrillar component (DFC), and the granular component (GC).
source: Nucleolar anatomy in animal cells is comprised of three distinct compartments: the fibrillar center (FC), the dense fibrillar component (DFC), and the granular component (GC) (Pederson, 2011).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: FC is the site of transcription that consists of rDNA and its associated transcription machinery such as transcription factor UBF and RNA Pol I.
source: FC is the site of transcription that consists of rDNA and its associated transcription machinery such as transcription factor UBF and RNA Pol I.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about nucleolar compartments.

claim: The DFC is the site of pre-rRNA processing distinguished by early RNA processing factors such as fibrillarin.
source: The DFC is the site of pre-rRNA processing distinguished by early RNA processing factors such as fibrillarin.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about nucleolar compartments.

claim: The GC contains proteins involved in late rRNA processing and assembly of pre-ribosomal particles and is marked by proteins such as nucleolin and nucleophosmin (NPM1).
source: The GC contains proteins involved in late rRNA processing and assembly of pre-ribosomal particles. It is marked by proteins such as nucleolin and nucleophosmin (NPM1).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about nucleolar compartments.

claim: Inhibition of RNA Pol I causes the reorganization of rDNA arrays and associated FC proteins into round nucleoli with peripheral 'stress caps.'
source: Changes in nucleolar organization during stress have not been studied extensively, except for the inhibition of RNA Pol I that causes the reorganization of rDNA arrays and associated FC proteins into round nucleoli with peripheral 'stress caps.'
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about nucleolar stress responses.

claim: Treatment with CX-5461 induced UBF condensation at the periphery of the nucleolar remnants and the formation of stress caps.
source: In cells expressing eGFP-UBF, treatment with CX-5461 induced UBF condensation at the periphery of the nucleolar remnants and the formation of stress caps (Figure 1B and Video 2).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 1B and Video 2.

claim: The average intensity of eGFP-nucleolin decreased in the nucleoli and increased in the nucleoplasm within the first hour after CX-5461 treatment.
source: With the first hour after treatment, the average intensity of eGFP-nucleolin decreased in the nucleoli and increased in the nucleoplasm (Figure 1A, right panel), indicating a higher proportion of total nucleolin dissolved in the nucleoplasm.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative imaging data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The intensity of eGFP-UBF increased in stress caps after CX-5461 treatment, while the intensity in the nucleoplasm did not change.
source: The intensity of eGFP-UBF increased in these small stress caps, while the intensity in the nucleoplasm did not change (Figure 1B, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative imaging data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Nucleolin became more mobile in stressed cells, with the average half-time recovery T1/2 decreasing from 4.58 ± 1.88 s to 2.89 ± 0.88 s after CX-5461 treatment.
source: Nucleolin became more mobile in stressed cells (the average half-time recovery T1/2 went down from 4.58 ± 1.88 s to 2.89 ± 0.88 s, Figure 1C), consistent with its redistribution to the nucleoplasm.
evidence: This is supported by FRAP analysis data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The T1/2 of UBF did not significantly change with stress and stayed on the average of 12–14 s.
source: The T1/2 of UBF did not significantly change with stress and stayed on the average of 12–14 s (Figure 1D), indicating that the rDNA-binding properties of UBF that likely underlie its FRAP behavior were not affected by RNA Pol I inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by FRAP analysis data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: UBF acts as a stable bookmark of the rDNA during mitosis, when RNA Pol I activity is very low.
source: This is consistent with UBF acting as a stable bookmark of the rDNA during mitosis, when RNA Pol I activity is very low (Roussel et al., 1993; Gébrane-Younès et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Of 1180 compounds present in the library, 12.9% were hits.
source: Of 1180 compounds present in the library, 12.9% were hits.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the screening study.

claim: 7% of the compounds in the library were hits at both 1 and 10 µM, and 5.8% were hits only at 10 µM.
source: Also, 7% of the compounds in the library were hits at both 1 and 10 µM, and 5.8% were hits only at 10 µM (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the screening study shown in Figure 2B.

claim: All hits in the screen had normality scores lower than the control.
source: All hits in the screen had normality scores lower than the control, that is, this parameter only went down, not up, in drug-treated cells.
evidence: This is an observation from the screening data.

claim: The number of cells in hit wells was typically lower than in control wells, indicating that the majority of drugs that induced nucleolar stress were cytostatic or cytotoxic.
source: The number of cells in hit wells was typically lower than in control wells, indicating that the majority of drugs that induced nucleolar stress were cytostatic or cytotoxic (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an observation from the screening data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: BMH-21 induced a 7.7-fold reduction in the normality score and a 2-fold reduction in cell number compared to DMSO control.
source: Cells treated with BMH-21 showed a 7.7-fold reduction in the normality score and a 2-fold reduction in cell number compared to DMSO control (highlighted in Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the screening study shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Inhibitors of mTOR and PI3 kinase had the highest frequency among all hits.
source: Grouping hits by drug target showed that inhibitors of mTOR and PI3 kinase had the highest frequency among all hits.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the screening data analysis.

claim: The most significantly enriched targets (p<0.001) were HSP90, mTOR, PI3K, and topoisomerase inhibitors.
source: The most significantly enriched targets (p<0.001) were HSP90, mTOR, PI3K, and topoisomerase inhibitors.
evidence: This is a statistical analysis result from the screening data.

claim: All compounds in the validation panel caused a significant reduction in nucleolar normality scores in all cell lines tested.
source: Nonetheless, all compounds caused a significant reduction in nucleolar normality scores in all cell lines (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a validation result shown in Figure 2F.

claim: All drugs in the panel caused a decrease in 5-EU incorporation, but to varying degrees.
source: All drugs in the panel caused a decrease in 5-EU incorporation, but to varying degrees.
evidence: This is supported by 5-EU incorporation assay data.

claim: There was a trend for drugs with lower normality scores to have lower rRNA synthesis, but it was not statistically significant.
source: Correlation analysis with normality scores showed that there was a trend for drugs with lower normality scores to have lower rRNA synthesis, but it was not statistically significant (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis result shown in Figure 3B.

claim: All DNA intercalating topoisomerase poison hits caused nucleolar shrinkage, rounding, and the canonical stress caps associated with RNA Pol I inhibition.
source: All DNA intercalating topoisomerase poison hits caused nucleolar shrinkage, rounding, and the canonical stress caps associated with RNA Pol I inhibition.
evidence: This is an observation from the characterization studies.

claim: Actinomycin D and CX-5461 can also poison the action of topoisomerases.
source: Notably, actinomycin D and CX-5461 can also poison the action of topoisomerases (Trask and Muller, 1988; Bruno et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: HSP90 inhibitor 17-AAG caused mild rDNA and UBF condensation that resembled the formation of stress caps but was less severe.
source: HSP90 inhibitor 17-AAG caused mild rDNA and UBF condensation that resembled the formation of stress caps but was less severe.
evidence: This is an observation from immuno-FISH experiments.

claim: Misfolded proteins can accumulate in the nucleolus upon heat shock.
source: It was recently shown that misfolded proteins can accumulate in the nucleolus upon heat shock (Azkanaz et al., 2019; Frottin et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Many nucleoli in carfilzomib-treated cells contained a diffuse pool of UBF not associated with the rDNA.
source: The nucleolar stress phenotype induced by proteasome inhibitor carfilzomib was similar to that of 17-AAG, except that many nucleoli contained a diffuse pool of UBF not associated with the rDNA (Figure 3C, arrow).
evidence: This is an observation from immuno-FISH experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Proteasome inhibition causes nucleolar accumulation of polyubiquitinated proteins, termed aggresomes.
source: Proteasome inhibition was previously shown to cause nucleolar accumulation of polyubiquitinated proteins, termed aggresomes (Latonen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: UBF can be ubiquitinated.
source: In addition, UBF itself can be ubiquitinated (Liu et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In CDK inhibitor-treated cells, the rDNA/UBF scaffold extended into undulant fibers, while nucleolin fully dispersed in the nucleoplasm.
source: In CDK inhibitor-treated cells, this scaffold extended into undulant fibers, while nucleolin fully dispersed in the nucleoplasm.
evidence: This is an observation from immuno-FISH experiments.

claim: Within 2–3 hr after flavopiridol addition, eGFP-nucleolin became dispersed in the nucleoplasm forming many small round droplets within the diffused pool.
source: Within 2–3 hr after flavopiridol addition, eGFP-nucleolin became dispersed in the nucleoplasm forming many small round droplets within the diffused pool (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and Video 3).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and Video 3.

claim: Flavopiridol treatment induced UBF decompaction into dotted strings with some diffusion into the nucleoplasm.
source: In cells expressing eGFP-UBF, flavopiridol treatment induced UBF decompaction into dotted strings with some diffusion into the nucleoplasm (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and Video 4).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and Video 4.

claim: The effect of flavopiridol on nucleoli was fully reversible within 4–6 hr after the inhibitor was washed out.
source: This effect was not consistent with apoptosis or necrosis, and it was fully reversible within 4–6 hr after the inhibitor was washed out (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and Video 5).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and Video 5.

claim: In flavopiridol-treated cells, POLR1A association with rDNA was reduced by nearly 70%.
source: In flavopiridol-treated cells, this association was reduced by nearly 70% (Figure 3D and E, Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: The total cellular amount of POLR1A protein did not decrease with any of the drug treatments.
source: The total cellular amount of POLR1A protein did not decrease with any of the drug treatments (Figure 3F), indicating that the loss of POLR1A association with rDNA in flavopiridol was not due to its degradation.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: CDK9 is the important kinase that phosphorylates the C-terminal domain (CTD) of RNA Pol II to control transcription initiation, elongation, and termination.
source: For RNA Pol II transcription, CDK9 is the important kinase that phosphorylates the C-terminal domain (CTD) to control transcription initiation, elongation, and termination (Bacon and D'Orso, 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: RNA Pol I lacks a CTD, and currently there are no known CDK-related mechanisms that control RNA Pol I.
source: RNA Pol I lacks a CTD, and currently there are no known CDK-related mechanisms that control RNA Pol I.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about RNA Pol I.

claim: Cells treated with AZD4573, JSH-150, and MC180295 showed an extended rDNA/UBF scaffold and dispersed nucleolin analogous to flavopiridol-treated cells.
source: Cells treated with AZD4573, JSH-150, and MC180295 showed an extended rDNA/UBF scaffold and dispersed nucleolin analogous to flavopiridol-treated cells (Figure 4A), suggesting that the nucleolar stress was likely induced by inhibition of CDK9.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: α-amanitin did not mimic the effects of CDK inhibitors and only caused a minor reduction in the normality score.
source: Importantly, α-amanitin did not mimic these effects and only caused a minor reduction in the normality score, indicating that catalytic inhibition of RNA Pol II alone was insufficient to cause the nucleolar stress phenotype observed with pan-CDK and CDK9-specific inhibitors.
evidence: This is supported by normality score measurements.

claim: Production of nascent RNA was decreased by 70–80% in all CDK inhibitors as measured by incorporation of 5-EU.
source: Production of nascent RNA, most of which is rRNA, was decreased by 70–80% in all CDK inhibitors as measured by incorporation of 5-EU (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by 5-EU incorporation data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: α-amanitin treatment did not cause a significant decrease in total rRNA.
source: α-Amanitin treatment did not cause a significant decrease in total rRNA (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by Y10b antibody labeling data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: In flavopiridol-treated cells, POLR1A association with rDNA was reduced by ~70%, and in CDK9 inhibitors it was reduced by ~60%.
source: In flavopiridol-treated cells, POLR1A association with rDNA was reduced by ~70%, and in CDK9 inhibitors it was reduced by ~60% (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: The effect of α-amanitin on the association of POLR1A with rDNA was much smaller (20%).
source: The effect of α-amanitin on the association of POLR1A with rDNA was much smaller (20%).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification.

claim: 148 proteins with peptides that had lower phosphorylation in both CDK inhibitor treatments were detected.
source: We detected 148 proteins with peptides that had lower phosphorylation in both treatments (Figure 5C, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Out of 148 proteins with lower phosphorylation after treatment with CDK inhibitors, 27 were nucleolar proteins.
source: Out of 148 proteins with lower phosphorylation after treatment with CDK inhibitors, 27 were nucleolar proteins (Figure 5C, denoted by yellow circles).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The Ki-67 protein had lower phosphorylation on four sites after CDK inhibitor treatment and became speckled throughout the nucleus.
source: For instance, the Ki-67 protein implicated in organizing heterochromatin around the nucleolus (Sobecki et al., 2016) had lower phosphorylation on four sites and became speckled throughout the nucleus (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by phosphoproteomics data and immunofluorescence shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Treacle was shown to be involved in rDNA transcription by connecting UBF and Pol I.
source: Treacle was shown to be involved in rDNA transcription by connecting UBF and Pol I (Valdez et al., 2004), and was also reported to recruit Pol I machinery independently of UBF (Lin and Yeh, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: CDK9/cyclin K effectively phosphorylated recombinant Treacle in vitro.
source: CDK9/cyclin K effectively phosphorylated recombinant Treacle in vitro (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: CDK9 did not phosphorylate purified RNA Pol I holoenzyme.
source: In line with the phosphoproteomics analysis, CDK9 did not phosphorylate purified RNA Pol I holoenzyme (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Treacle localization to the fibrillar center of the nucleolus together with UBF was unaffected in cells treated with CDK inhibitors.
source: Treacle localized to the fibrillar center of the nucleolus together with UBF in untreated cells. This localization was unaffected in cells treated with CDK inhibitors (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Anti-Treacle antibody efficiently pulled down POLR1A from lysates of cells treated with vehicle or Pol I inhibitor CX-5461, but not from cells treated with pan-CDK inhibitor flavopiridol or CDK9-specific inhibitors AZD4573 and JSH-150.
source: Anti-Treacle antibody efficiently pulled down POLR1A from lysates of cells treated with vehicle or Pol I inhibitor CX-5461, but not from cells treated with pan-CDK inhibitor flavopiridol or CDK9-specific inhibitors AZD4573 and JSH-150 (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation and western blot data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: There was no significant difference in the recovery rate between fully bleached and partially bleached nucleoli for NPM1-GFP.
source: There was no significant difference in the recovery rate between fully bleached and partially bleached nucleoli (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is supported by FRAP analysis data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: The average recovery rate (T1/2) of NPM1-GFP was ~28 ± 9.9 s for fully bleached nucleoli and ~24 ± 7.8 s for partially bleached nucleoli in untreated cells.
source: The average recovery rate (T1/2) was ~28 ± 9.9 s for fully bleached nucleoli and ~24 ± 7.8 s for partially bleached nucleoli.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from FRAP analysis.

claim: In cells with more than one nucleolus, as the photobleached part gained and the unbleached part expended fluorescence, the separate, unconnected nucleoli also lost fluorescence at a comparable rate.
source: In cells with more than one nucleolus, the partial bleach analysis revealed that as the photobleached part gained and the unbleached part expended fluorescence, the separate, unconnected nucleoli also lost fluorescence at a comparable rate (an example is shown in Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by FRAP analysis data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Treatment with the RNA Pol I inhibitor CX-5461 caused NPM1-GFP to concentrate inside the nucleolar remnants.
source: Treatment with the RNA Pol I inhibitor CX-5461 caused NPM1-GFP to concentrate inside the nucleolar remnants (Figure 6D and Video 6).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 6D and Video 6.

claim: CDK inhibitor treatment triggered the dispersal of the NPM1-GFP into multiple small globules and increased the diffuse pool in the nucleoplasm.
source: In contrast, CDK inhibitor treatment triggered the dispersal of the NPM1-GFP into multiple small globules and increased the diffuse pool in the nucleoplasm (Figure 6E and Video 7).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 6E and Video 7.

claim: FRAP analysis of whole nucleoli in RNA Pol I inhibitor-treated cells demonstrated an ~2.5-fold increase in the recovery rate compared to the untreated cells.
source: FRAP analysis of whole nucleoli in RNA Pol I inhibitor-treated cells demonstrated an ~2.5-fold increase in the recovery rate compared to the untreated cells (Figure 6F and G), indicating a higher exchange rate of NPM1 molecules between the nucleolar remnants and the nucleoplasm and/or lower nucleolar viscosity.
evidence: This is supported by FRAP analysis data shown in Figure 6F and G.

claim: In CDK inhibitor-treated cells, photobleached NPM1-GFP globules recovered with T1/2 ~6.9 ± 2.4 s.
source: In CDK inhibitor-treated cells, photobleached NPM1-GFP globules recovered even faster (T1/2 ~6.9 ± 2.4 s) (Figure 6F and G) at a rate comparable to nucleoplasm (T1/2 ~6 ± 1.7 s, Figure 6H).
evidence: This is supported by FRAP analysis data shown in Figure 6F, G, and H.

claim: Nucleolar organization is more complex than predicted by multicomponent LLPS alone.
source: Our interpretation of these results is that nucleolar organization, normal or during stress, is more complex than predicted by multicomponent LLPS alone.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the FRAP analysis results.

claim: Transcriptional activity is strongly correlated with nucleolar integrity and impacts a large number of protein–protein and protein–nucleic acid interactions.
source: Transcriptional activity is strongly correlated with nucleolar integrity and impacts a large number of protein–protein and protein–nucleic acid interactions, some of which occur through specific binding while others are driven by phase separation (Tartakoff et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The combination of both specific binding and phase separation modes of interaction is likely required for the formation and function of the nucleolus.
source: The combination of both modes of interaction is likely required for the formation and function of the nucleolus.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Nucleolar stress can manifest in different forms depending on the biological pathway or pathways targeted by a particular drug.
source: Our results show that nucleolar stress can manifest in different forms depending on the biological pathway or pathways targeted by a particular drug (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the study shown in Figure 7.

claim: Inhibition of mTOR and PI3K growth pathways resulted in a decrease in nucleolar normality score and rRNA synthesis without dramatic reorganization of nucleolar anatomy.
source: Inhibition of mTOR and PI3K growth pathways resulted in a decrease in nucleolar normality score and rRNA synthesis without dramatic reorganization of nucleolar anatomy.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the characterization studies.

claim: Inhibitors of HSP90 and the proteasome caused proteotoxic stress – acute loss of protein homeostasis.
source: Inhibitors of HSP90 and the proteasome caused proteotoxic stress – acute loss of protein homeostasis.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the characterization studies.

claim: The most extreme nucleolar stress in the screen was caused by CDK inhibitors.
source: The most extreme nucleolar stress in our screen was caused by CDK inhibitors.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the screening study.

claim: Constitutive CDK activity is necessary for the assembly of functional RNA Pol I transcriptional complexes and the integrity of the nucleolar compartment.
source: Rapid nucleolar disintegration implied that constitutive CDK activity is necessary for the assembly of functional RNA Pol I transcriptional complexes and the integrity of the nucleolar compartment.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Flavopiridol was previously shown to impede rRNA production and processing.
source: CDK inhibitor flavopiridol was previously shown to impede rRNA production and processing (Burger et al., 2010; Burger et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A recent study attributed the disruptive effect of flavopiridol on RNA Pol I transcription to its inhibition of RNA Pol II.
source: A recent study attributed the disruptive effect of flavopiridol on RNA Pol I transcription to its inhibition of RNA Pol II (Abraham et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The absence of nucleolar disruption in cells treated with the catalytic RNA Pol II-specific inhibitor α-amanitin suggests that the disruptive effect of flavopiridol on RNA Pol I transcription is not due to inhibition of RNA Pol II.
source: The absence of nucleolar disruption in cells treated with the catalytic RNA Pol II-specific inhibitor α-amanitin suggests otherwise.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Transcriptional CDK activity may affect nucleolar function directly.
source: Our phosphoproteomics analysis identified multiple nucleolar CDK substrates, arguing that transcriptional CDK activity may affect nucleolar function directly.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the phosphoproteomics data.

claim: The phosphorylation of Treacle, possibly by CDK9, plays a significant role in recruiting Pol I machinery to the rDNA to facilitate Pol I transcription.
source: These results suggest that the phosphorylation of Treacle, possibly by CDK9, plays a significant role in recruiting Pol I machinery to the rDNA to facilitate Pol I transcription.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Transcriptional CDKs drive the RNA production for both RNA Pol I and RNA Pol II, offering a coordination mechanism for ribosome biogenesis.
source: The idea that transcriptional CDKs drive the RNA production for both RNA Pol I and RNA Pol II offers a coordination mechanism for ribosome biogenesis that requires products of both mRNA and rRNA genes.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: All CDK inhibitor hits in the screen that had low normality scores were pan-CDK inhibitors.
source: All CDK inhibitor hits in our screen that had low normality scores were pan-CDK inhibitors.
evidence: This is an observation from the screening data.

claim: CDK inhibitors more specific to key cell cycle CDKs (RO3306, BMS265246, PD0332991, LY2835219, LEE011) were not hits in the screen.
source: The anticancer compound library also contained CDK inhibitors that were more specific to key cell cycle CDKs: RO3306 (CDK1), BMS265246 (CDK1/2), PD0332991 – palbociclib, LY2835219 – abemaciclib, and LEE011 – ribociclib (CDK4/6). These drugs were not hits in our screen, indicating that the nucleolar stress caused by pan-CDK inhibitors may not be a result of inhibiting cell cycle CDKs.
evidence: This is an observation from the screening data.

claim: The nucleolus is targeted by many anticancer compounds, whether intentional or not.
source: The results of our screen demonstrate that the nucleolus is targeted by many anticancer compounds, whether intentional or not.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the screening study.

claim: For drugs that cause nucleolar stress, their antiproliferative activity can be at least in part attributed to disrupting nucleolar processes.
source: For drugs that cause nucleolar stress, their antiproliferative activity can be at least in part attributed to disrupting nucleolar processes.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Unintended nucleolar stress can be a source of toxicity.
source: Unintended nucleolar stress can also be a source of toxicity.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: CX-5461 arrests Pol I at the rDNA promoter, which blocks transcription initiation.
source: This drug has been shown to arrest Pol I at the rDNA promoter, which blocks transcription initiation (Mars et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BMH-21 intercalates in the DNA and binds strongly to GC-rich rDNA, repressing RNA Pol I transcription.
source: BMH-21 intercalates in the DNA and binds strongly to GC-rich rDNA, repressing RNA Pol I transcription (Colis et al., 2014; Wei et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Ribosomal RNA can account for ~80% of the total cellular RNA.
source: Since ribosomal RNA can account for ~80% of the total cellular RNA (Palazzo and Lee, 2015), the total amount of nascent RNA approximates the synthesis of ribosomal RNA.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: mTOR and PI3K are metabolic pathways that positively regulate ribosome biogenesis on multiple levels including rDNA transcription.
source: mTOR and PI3K are metabolic pathways that positively regulate ribosome biogenesis on multiple levels including rDNA transcription (Mayer and Grummt, 2006; Pelletier et al., 2018), so the strong (~60%) reduction in 5-EU incorporation in mTOR inhibitor sapanisertib and PI3K inhibitor taselicib was predictable.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: rDNA transcription may be hypersensitive to DNA intercalators in general.
source: rDNA transcription may be hypersensitive to DNA intercalators in general (Andrews et al., 2021), and for many DNA intercalating drugs the nucleolar stress cap phenotype is well-characterized (Ferreira et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: 17-AAG blocks the ATP-binding pocket of molecular chaperone HSP90, leading to the accumulation of misfolded proteins.
source: 17-AAG blocks the ATP-binding pocket of molecular chaperone HSP90, leading to the accumulation of misfolded proteins (Trepel et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Carfilzomib inhibits the chymotrypsin-like activity of the 20S proteasome, blocking the degradation of poly-ubiquitinated proteins.
source: Carfilzomib inhibits the chymotrypsin-like activity of the 20S proteasome, blocking the degradation of poly-ubiquitinated proteins (Orlowski and Kuhn, 2008).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Flavopiridol is an ATP-competitive inhibitor of CDKs and can be considered a pan-CDK inhibitor.
source: Flavopiridol is an ATP-competitive inhibitor of CDKs and can be considered a pan-CDK inhibitor (Senderowicz, 1999).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The human genome encodes 21 CDKs.
source: The human genome encodes 21 CDKs, some of which have been studied extensively while others remain cryptic.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Transcriptional CDKs drive the activity of RNA polymerase II (CDK8, CDK9, CDK12, CDK19).
source: Transcriptional CDKs drive the activity of RNA polymerase II (CDK8, CDK9, CDK12, CDK19).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: The RNA Pol II inhibitor α-amanitin induced a small (~10%) but significant decrease in 5-EU incorporation.
source: The RNA Pol II inhibitor α-amanitin induced a small (~10%) but significant decrease in 5-EU incorporation, which was expected because 5-EU is also incorporated in RNA Pol II transcripts.
evidence: This is supported by 5-EU incorporation data.

claim: Y10b antibody labeling showed 45–55% decrease in total rRNA in CDK inhibitor-treated cells.
source: To examine the amount of rRNA by another method, we measured the total amount of rRNA by Y10b (anti-rRNA) antibody fluorescence. Y10b antibody labeling showed 45–55% decrease in total rRNA that was comparable in all CDK inhibitors.
evidence: This is supported by Y10b antibody labeling data.

claim: CDK inhibition reduces rRNA production by causing the disassociation of RNA Pol I from the rDNA, and not through a secondary effect of inhibition of RNA Pol II.
source: These data suggest that CDK inhibition reduces rRNA production by causing the disassociation of RNA Pol I from the rDNA, and not through a secondary effect of inhibition of RNA Pol II.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Transcriptional CDK activity, potentially CDK9, is necessary for RNA Pol I activity and nucleolar integrity.
source: Our data further suggest that transcriptional CDK activity, potentially CDK9, is necessary for RNA Pol I activity and nucleolar integrity.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: 61 enriched and 22 depleted proteins were identified in both CDK inhibitor treatments.
source: The total protein abundance analysis identified 61 enriched and 22 depleted proteins in both drug treatments (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the proteomics analysis shown in Figure 2B (likely Figure 5B based on context).

claim: Among commonly enriched proteins with the highest fold change was the stress-induced transcription factor p53.
source: Among commonly enriched proteins with the highest fold change was the stress-induced transcription factor p53.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the proteomics analysis.

claim: The tumor suppressor protein p53 has previously been shown to accumulate in flavopiridol-treated cells by multiple studies.
source: The tumor suppressor protein p53 has previously been shown to accumulate in flavopiridol-treated cells by multiple studies (Shapiro et al., 1999; Alonso et al., 2003; Demidenko and Blagosklonny, 2004), confirming our quantitative proteomics results.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The commonly depleted group of proteins included ribosome biogenesis factors RPF1, RRP36, and DDX56.
source: The commonly depleted group of proteins included ribosome biogenesis factors RPF1, RRP36, and DDX56.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the proteomics analysis.

claim: Multiple identified phosphosites belonged to POLR2A, the catalytic subunit of RNA polymerase II (Pol II).
source: Most of the phosphorylation sites were serines and threonines. Multiple identified phosphosites belonged to POLR2A, the catalytic subunit of RNA polymerase II (Pol II).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis.

claim: CDK9 phosphorylates the CTD of POLR2A on multiple residues, controlling transcription initiation, elongation, and recruitment of the splicing machinery.
source: In particular, CDK9 phosphorylates the CTD on multiple residues, controlling transcription initiation, elongation, and recruitment of the splicing machinery (Eick and Geyer, 2013; Guo et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Differentially phosphorylated POLR2A peptides for eight C-terminal residues were recovered.
source: We recovered differentially phosphorylated POLR2A peptides for eight C-terminal residues (Figure 5C, red rings), validating this approach for detecting CDK substrates.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Mutations in TCOF1 cause Treacher Collins syndrome, a congenital craniofacial disorder associated with tissue-specific disruptions in ribosome biogenesis.
source: Mutations in TCOF1 cause Treacher Collins syndrome, a congenital craniofacial disorder associated with tissue-specific disruptions in ribosome biogenesis (Sakai and Trainor, 2009; Noack Watt et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Treacle is a large nucleolar protein containing multiple low-complexity regions with alternating acidic and basic tracts in its central disordered region.
source: Treacle is a large nucleolar protein containing multiple low-complexity regions with alternating acidic and basic tracts in its central disordered region (Grzanka and Piekiełko-Witkowska, 2021).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Treacle is a phosphoprotein that contains numerous serine and threonine residues within its central disordered domain.
source: Treacle is a phosphoprotein that contains numerous serine and threonine residues within its central disordered domain, but the functional significance of this phosphorylation is unknown.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: The phosphorylation of Treacle decreased when cells were treated with CDK inhibitors.
source: The phosphorylation of Treacle decreased when cells were treated with CDK inhibitors.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the phosphoproteomics analysis.

claim: CDK9 can directly phosphorylate Treacle and RNA Pol II, but not RNA Pol I.
source: Therefore, CDK9 can directly phosphorylate Treacle and RNA Pol II, but not RNA Pol I.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on in vitro kinase assay data.

claim: Western blotting of whole-cell lysates did not show the degradation of Treacle or POLR1A in any drug treatments.
source: Western blotting of whole-cell lysates did not show the degradation of Treacle or POLR1A in any drug treatments.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data.

claim: Inhibition of CDK9 creates an extreme form of nucleolar stress where only the bare rDNA scaffold with few associated proteins remains.
source: In summary, inhibition of CDK9 creates an extreme form of nucleolar stress where only the bare rDNA scaffold with few associated proteins remains.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the study.

claim: The subunits of the Pol I machinery dissociate from rDNA, potentially due in part to the dephosphorylation of Treacle.
source: The subunits of the Pol I machinery dissociate from rDNA, potentially due in part to the dephosphorylation of Treacle.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Transcriptional CDK activity must be necessary for maintaining rDNA transcription and nucleolar integrity.
source: Thus, transcriptional CDK activity must be necessary for maintaining rDNA transcription and nucleolar integrity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: NPM1 is a multifunctional nucleolar protein involved in the assembly of ribosomal subunits that occupies the granular component (GC) of the nucleolus.
source: NPM1 is a multifunctional nucleolar protein involved in the assembly of ribosomal subunits that occupies the granular component (GC) of the nucleolus.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about NPM1.

claim: NPM1 contains an N-terminal oligomerization domain, a C-terminal RNA-binding domain, an intrinsically disordered region (IDR), and multiple acidic tracts throughout the protein.
source: It contains an N-terminal oligomerization domain, a C-terminal RNA-binding domain, an intrinsically disordered region (IDR), and multiple acidic tracts throughout the protein.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about NPM1 structure.

claim: NPM1 forms a homopentamer, binds rRNA, and can form multivalent interactions with other proteins that contain arginine-rich domains.
source: It forms a homopentamer, binds rRNA, and can form multivalent interactions with other proteins that contain arginine-rich domains.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about NPM1 function.

claim: Studies of IDR-containing proteins including NPM1 demonstrated that these proteins can form homotypic and heterotypic interactions that drive liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS).
source: Studies of IDR-containing proteins including NPM1 demonstrated that these proteins can form homotypic and heterotypic interactions that drive liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS), which has been proposed to play a role in the assembly of membrane-less organelles such as the nucleolus (Feric et al., 2016; Mitrea et al., 2018; Lafontaine et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: For a classical phase-separated liquid condensate, the recovery time of a partially bleached structure is expected to be faster than the recovery of the entire structure due to rapid internal molecular rearrangements.
source: For a classical phase-separated liquid condensate, the recovery time of a partially bleached structure was expected to be faster than the recovery of the entire structure due to rapid internal molecular rearrangements (Brangwynne et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Nucleolar and nucleoplasmic pools of NPM1 both contributed to the recovery process, and the diffusion within the nucleolus does not necessarily dominate the exchange with nucleoplasm as would be expected of a prototypical phase-separated condensate.
source: This implied that nucleolar and nucleoplasmic pools of NPM1 both contributed to the recovery process, and the diffusion within the nucleolus does not necessarily dominate the exchange with nucleoplasm as would be expected of a prototypical phase-separated condensate.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the FRAP analysis results.

claim: NPM1-GFP globules in CDK inhibitor-treated cells did not merge over time despite being in close proximity and being quite mobile.
source: Although NPM1-GFP globules had the appearance of classic phase-separated droplets, they did not merge over time despite being in close proximity and being quite mobile.
evidence: This is an observation from live cell imaging.

claim: The rapid exchange rate of NPM1-GFP in CDK inhibitor-treated cells suggests very weak interactions of NPM1 molecules with the components of these globules.
source: This rapid exchange rate suggests very weak interactions of NPM1 molecules with the components of these globules.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the FRAP analysis results.

claim: NPM1 dynamics in RNA Pol I inhibitor-treated cells were consistent with a compromised but extant nucleolar GC layer.
source: Overall, NPM1 dynamics in RNA Pol I inhibitor-treated cells were consistent with a compromised but extant nucleolar GC layer, while in CDK inhibitor-treated cells they were in line with GC disassembly.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the FRAP analysis results.

claim: NPM1 dynamics in CDK inhibitor-treated cells were in line with GC disassembly.
source: Overall, NPM1 dynamics in RNA Pol I inhibitor-treated cells were consistent with a compromised but extant nucleolar GC layer, while in CDK inhibitor-treated cells they were in line with GC disassembly.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the FRAP analysis results.

claim: Understanding nucleolar stress phenotypes observed in this study from a biophysical perspective will require moving beyond current models that rely solely on phase separation as the basis for nucleolar assembly.
source: Understanding nucleolar stress phenotypes observed in this study from a biophysical perspective will require moving beyond current models that rely solely on phase separation as the basis for nucleolar assembly.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: The canonical nucleolar stress caused by DNA intercalating agents and manifested by the segregation of stress caps was only one nucleolar stress phenotype.
source: The canonical nucleolar stress caused by DNA intercalating agents and manifested by the segregation of stress caps was only one nucleolar stress phenotype.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the study.

claim: The response to mTOR and PI3K inhibition may not represent stress per se, but a consequence of the overall downregulation of ribosome biogenesis processes.
source: This response may not represent stress per se, but a consequence of the overall downregulation of ribosome biogenesis processes (Iadevaia et al., 2012; Davis et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Accumulation of misfolded and/or undegraded proteins may impair nucleolar functions directly, by clogging its compartments and creating 'aggresome'-based nucleolar stress.
source: Accumulation of misfolded and/or undegraded proteins may impair nucleolar functions directly, by clogging its compartments and creating 'aggresome'-based nucleolar stress (Frottin et al., 2019), and/or indirectly, by suppressing growth signaling through metabolic pathways (Su and Dai, 2017; Guang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Nucleoli are often used by pathologists to predict cancer aggressiveness.
source: Nucleoli are often used by pathologists to predict cancer aggressiveness; our studies extend the ability to use nucleolar morphology as a biomarker of underlying cellular state.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: The studies extend the ability to use nucleolar morphology as a biomarker of underlying cellular state.
source: Nucleoli are often used by pathologists to predict cancer aggressiveness; our studies extend the ability to use nucleolar morphology as a biomarker of underlying cellular state.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study findings.

claim: A recent large-scale proteomic study identified multiple nucleolar proteins as targets of CDK9.
source: Our findings are consistent with a recent large-scale proteomic study that identified multiple nucleolar proteins as targets of CDK9 (Johnson et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Cell cycle CDKs drive concerted processes of DNA replication and mitosis by phosphorylating multiple substrates.
source: The same theme of overarching regulation is typical for cell cycle CDKs that drive concerted processes of DNA replication and mitosis by phosphorylating multiple substrates.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about cell cycle CDKs.

claim: Developing inhibitors that target a particular CDK with high specificity is challenging due to the presence of multiple transcriptional CDKs in the human genome that share nearly identical ATP-binding pockets.
source: Developing inhibitors that target a particular CDK with high specificity is challenging due to the presence of multiple transcriptional CDKs in the human genome that share nearly identical ATP-binding pockets, the sites targeted by ATP-competitive inhibitors (Jorda et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The nucleolar stress caused by pan-CDK inhibitors may not be a result of inhibiting cell cycle CDKs.
source: These drugs were not hits in our screen, indicating that the nucleolar stress caused by pan-CDK inhibitors may not be a result of inhibiting cell cycle CDKs.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the screening data.

claim: The entire cell cycle can run on just CDK1 in the absence of other CDKs in mouse and yeast.
source: This aspect of CDK biology is better explored for cell cycle CDKs – for instance, mouse and yeast knockout studies showed that the entire cell cycle can run on just CDK1 in the absence of other CDKs (Kozar and Sicinski, 2005; Santamaría et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The ability of related transcriptional CDKs to functionally compensate for each other and/or perform redundant functions has not been well-explored.
source: The ability of related transcriptional CDKs to functionally compensate for each other and/or perform redundant functions has not been well-explored.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of scientific knowledge.

claim: It is possible that other kinases can phosphorylate the same nucleolar substrates as CDK9 and their inhibition can cause similar nucleolar stress phenotype.
source: We allow the possibility that we may be targeting other kinases that can phosphorylate the same nucleolar substrates as CDK9 and their inhibition can cause similar nucleolar stress phenotype.
evidence: This is a speculative statement acknowledging limitations.

claim: While the results suggest that CDK9 activity plays a key role in rDNA transcription and nucleolar integrity, it is still possible that other transcriptional CDKs can perform similar functions.
source: Thus, while our results suggest that CDK9 activity plays a key role in rDNA transcription and nucleolar integrity, it is still possible that other transcriptional CDKs can perform similar functions.
evidence: This is a speculative statement acknowledging limitations.

claim: Therapeutic and mechanistic studies should consider nucleolar stress as a potential confounding factor in determining the mechanism of action and toxicity in drug development.
source: Therapeutic and mechanistic studies should consider nucleolar stress as a potential confounding factor in determining the mechanism of action and toxicity in drug development.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the study findings.
